summary: Runs StructCleanup (0x004BD800) over an 8x8 grid of element pointers whose stride is 9 pointer-sized slots, then performs one final StructCleanup on the base pointer advanced by 576 slots. The caller (Game_Post, 0x0042DA30) supplies the grid base. Both loop counters are hardcoded to 8 and the pointer advance is exactly 9 slots per iteration.

operations.description: Initialize the outer loop counter v3 to 8.
Outer countdown loop driven by v3; body runs 8 times while v3 is nonzero.
Initialize the inner loop counter v4 to 8.
Inner countdown loop driven by v4; body runs 8 times while v4 is nonzero.
Call StructCleanup(0x004BD800) on the current element pointer v2.
Advance the element pointer by 9 slots: v2 += 9 (element stride of 9 LPVOID-sized entries).
Decrement the inner counter v4 each inner iteration.
Decrement the outer counter v3 each outer iteration.
Final StructCleanup(0x004BD800) call on this + 576 (9 slots x 64 = 576), covering the remainder of the grid.
Return the result of the final StructCleanup call (raw decompiler keeps this as the function return).

unresolved: Element semantics and class of the 64 grid slots plus the trailing slot at this + 576 are unknown; StructCleanup takes the element pointer directly.
Whether the grid is an array of structs or an array of pointers is not resolvable from this function alone (advance is a compile-time pointer arithmetic constant of 9 LPVOID slots).
Purpose of the overall grid (why Game_Post triggers an 8x8 + trailing cleanup) is unknown.
